summary: annual interest rate is what the Effective interest rate calculator works out, and it gets there from the periodic rate, the effective interest rate (EIR) and the final balance. It is built for a budget, a loan conversation, a payslip check or a what-if before you talk to a lender. Nothing repaints underneath you: edit a field, press Calculate, and the new answer appears. That is how you find out which input the result is sensitive to.

sections.title: How does the Effective interest rate calculator work?
sections.html:
The Effective interest rate calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports annual interest rate in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you type in the periodic rate, the effective interest rate (EIR) (Interest rates), the final balance (Balances) and the final balance (Balances).

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Effective interest rate calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Annual interest rate=compounding frequency × ((effective interest rate (EIR) + 1 ^ 1 ÷ compounding frequency) − 1)
Annual interest rate=the natural log of (effective interest rate (EIR) + 1)
Annual interest rate=compounding frequency × ((final balance ÷ initial balance, 1 ÷ (compounding frequency × term)) − 1)
Annual interest rate=the natural log of (final balance ÷ initial balance) ÷ term
Compounding frequency=annual interest rate ÷ periodic rate

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • %, opening in percent
  • %, opening in percent
  • %, opening in percent
  • %, opening in percent
  • Time, opening in years / months
  • Currency, opening in US Dollar
  • Currency, opening in US Dollar
  • Currency, opening in US Dollar

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Effective interest rate calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Preparing questions for a lender, an accountant or an adviser
  • Comparing two offers that quote their costs in different ways
  • Sizing up a purchase before you commit to it
  • Any time the same 3 figures keep coming back — the periodic rate, the effective interest rate (EIR) and the final balance — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Effective interest rate calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns annual interest rate, derived from the periodic rate, the effective interest rate (EIR) and the final balance. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Effective interest rate calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the periodic rate, the effective interest rate (EIR) and the final balance, which is 4 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter annual interest rate in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Annual interest rate opens in percent and the chip beside it offers 6 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There is one choice to make (1 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

faq.q: Is the Effective interest rate calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
